assumption.claim: Omitting user_id should return items across all users; using an empty WHERE clause (i.e., no WHERE) correctly yields that behavior.

basis_summary: step 9 thought: The current handler silently substitutes a hard-coded user when `user_id` is absent, so I’m removing that fallback. I’m keeping the existing `items` response field and adding explicit page metadata so clients can navigate without breaking item parsing.
verdict: The agent assumed that omitting user_id and dropping the WHERE clause would safely return all user-owned items. In reality, the items table includes rows with user_id = NULL, so toDTO passed a null to ownerCode, which then called toString() on null and threw at owner.ts:6. This surfaced when rows.map(toDTO) executed in listItems at src/items.ts:67.
correction: When user_id is not provided, do not remove the WHERE clause entirely; instead, restrict results to owned items by using WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL. Build the SQL as: for a provided user_id, use WHERE user_id = ? with [userId, limit, offset]; otherwise use WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL with [limit, offset]. Apply the same condition to the COUNT(*) query so that toDTO/ownerCode never receives a null user identifier.
